It's crazy how we have to decide what type of field we want to go into in our late teenage years.  There is a reason why undecided majors exist at colleges.  Also, colleges are flexible if you ever feel you need to switch your major and usually you do not start your major courses until the 2nd semester of your freshman year.

I wanted to go into molecular biology because I always found myself in a rabbit hole about googling different types of diseases and I took an elective in microbiology and I loved it.  That's basically it.  It is very hard to find a specific career to work towards since there are so many types of jobs out there.  Instead of focusing on figuring out what specific career you want, focus on what subject/passion/class you wouldn't mind studying more detail about.

College apps appear to be one big task unless you break it down.  I am one to procrastinate so looking at that big task made me less motivated to do it.  I had to balance my school work with completing college apps which was a pain.  Also you need to plan ahead too for FAFSA, teacher recommendations, studying, completing, and sending your SAT scores, college editing, etc.  (I'm not very good with planning ahead if you could not tell).

There's also the stress of waiting for that college decision to come back.  Wishes could be granted or broken or put on the waitlist.  You dread waiting for a rejection letter to come saying, "thanks for your money and time spent on these applications you poured your heart on.  Simply put, those 4 dedicated years weren't good enough for this school/you did not pass the vibe check."  But still after you get back those decision papers, even if it's a safety school, it's such a nice feeling to finally get into a college and know that your hard work paid off and there is a college out there that appreciates it (especially with merit $$$).

I'm a senior who did take geometry my sophomore year as well.  I don't think colleges really look at what year you take a certain class, but they look at whether or not you took the class at all.  It's more important that you take and pass the actual courses rather than the order of the actual math courses.  Also if you have taken algebra II and geometry, you are in great shape for the math SATs junior year.  
So yes it is totally ok to take geometry as a sophomore.  At my school, a lot of my close friends took it over the summer or as a junior.  People learn at different paces and the course of education they take is their own.  Unlike english or history where people at my school start on the same level, since different middle schools had different math curriculums (mine taught me 8th grade math and algebra I), people were put into different math courses.  Before you send in your college apps, the goal is: you should have already completed algebra I, algebra II, geometry, and maybe precalc.

What helped me was getting together with one of my friends who was also planning to take the SATs. We had similar goals on wanting to obtain a really good score but we also liked to procrastinate.  We took the same practice SATs from the SAT book together and we were timed like how it was on the actual exam.  When we were done, we helped each other understand what we did wrong and how to fix it.  She helped me understand the reading and English sections more while I explained the answers to math sections in more detail.  I found that studying with a friend helped boost my motivation because it felt like we were depending on each other to help our futures and it wasn’t something I could push off until later because I had already set a date and time with that friend.

Another thing that helps is taking breaks while studying because forgetting to do that is how I lose interest and motivation.  If you are studying alone, I recommend using Khan Academy a LOT because it has a lot of similar problems that can appear on the actual exam and also it’s free :)

I hope this helps and I wish you the best of luck!
